title: Polygon Vocabulary Assessment
description: Classify polygon examples and non-examples, then use vocabulary about sides, vertices, diagonals, regular polygons, and irregular polygons.

questions.question: Which set of features is required for a figure to be a polygon?
options: Closed, flat, and made only of straight line segments
Open, flat, and made only of straight line segments
Closed, flat, and made with at least one curved side
Three-dimensional and made of flat faces
questions.explanation: A polygon is a closed plane figure made only of straight line segments.

questions.question: A figure has 5 straight sides, 5 vertices, and no gaps. What can you conclude?
options: It is not a polygon
It is a polygon
It must be regular
It must have a curved side
questions.explanation: The figure is closed and made of straight sides, so it is a polygon. More information is needed to decide if it is regular.

questions.question: A regular polygon must have all sides equal and all angles equal.
questions.explanation: Both conditions are required. Equal sides alone or equal angles alone is not enough for regularity.

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, which segment is a diagonal?
options: PQ
QR
RS
PR
questions.explanation: PR connects non-adjacent vertices, so it is a diagonal. PQ, QR, and RS are sides.

questions.question: The plural form of vertex is ____.
questions.explanation: More than one vertex is called vertices.

questions.question: Which statement describes an irregular polygon?
options: It is always open.
It always has a curved side.
It is a polygon that does not have all sides equal and all angles equal.
It is not allowed to have vertices.
questions.explanation: An irregular polygon is still a polygon, but it is not both equilateral and equiangular.

questions.question: A line segment connecting two adjacent vertices is a diagonal.
questions.explanation: A diagonal connects non-adjacent vertices. Adjacent vertices are connected by a side.

questions.question: Which object is most likely modeled by a polygon?
options: The circular face of a coin
The rectangular face of a book cover
The curved outline of an oval mirror
The spiral path of a spring
questions.explanation: A rectangle is a closed figure made of straight sides, so the face of a book cover can be modeled by a polygon.

questions.question: A learner says, "This shape is closed, but it has one curved side, so it is a polygon." Correct the learner's statement.
questions.correctAnswer: The shape is not a polygon because polygons must be made only of straight line segments. Being closed is not enough.
questions.explanation: A correct response should state that the curved side makes the figure a non-example of a polygon.

questions.question: Describe how you would check whether a drawn hexagon is regular.
questions.correctAnswer: Measure or compare all six side lengths and all six angles. The hexagon is regular only if all sides are equal and all angles are equal.
questions.explanation: Regularity requires checking both side lengths and angle measures, not just counting the number of sides.
